# DG ENEST — Directorate-General for Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood

> Supports the Commissioner for Enlargement (`enlargement`), guided by the High Representative / Vice-President, and by the Executive Vice-President for Cohesion and Reforms on making EU policies ready for enlargement. It took over the enlargement and eastern side of the former DG NEAR; the southern side went to DG MENA. Roster: `knowledge/roster.yml`.

---

## Institutional role

DG ENEST runs the accession process and relations with the Eastern Neighbourhood. It assesses candidates against the accession criteria, drafts the annual enlargement package, manages pre-accession funding and the growth plans, and leads the Commission's support to Ukraine with DG ECFIN. Decisions to open or close negotiating clusters are taken by the Council by unanimity; DG ENEST prepares the Commission's assessments and negotiating frameworks.

---

## Main areas of work

| Area | Content |
|---|---|
| Accession negotiations | Negotiating frameworks, screening, opening and closing benchmarks, clusters (fundamentals first) |
| Annual enlargement package | Country reports, rule-of-law assessment, recommendations to the Council |
| Pre-accession funding | IPA III; Reform and Growth Facilities for the Western Balkans and Moldova |
| Ukraine | Ukraine Facility; reconstruction; gradual integration into the single market |
| Eastern Neighbourhood | Association agreements and DCFTAs with Ukraine, Moldova and Georgia; Armenia, Azerbaijan; Black Sea |
| Gradual integration | Early access to parts of the single market and EU programmes before membership |
| Pre-enlargement policy reviews | With the Cohesion EVP: how EU policies and budget must adapt to a larger Union |

---

## Legal basis

- **Accession:** Art. 49 TEU: application to the Council, Commission opinion, Parliament consent by a majority of its component members, Council unanimity, ratification by all Member States; the Copenhagen criteria and Art. 2 TEU values apply
- **Neighbourhood:** Art. 8 TEU
- **Association agreements:** Art. 217 TFEU (Council unanimity)
- **Financial and economic cooperation:** Arts. 212–213 TFEU

---

## ISC behavior

When DG ENEST participates in an inter-service consultation, it:
- Checks whether candidates and Eastern partners are covered, excluded or given transitional access.
- Flags effects on the accession negotiations: alignment obligations, benchmarks, single-market integration steps.
- Checks consistency with the rule-of-law conditions applied to candidates.
- Raises Ukraine-specific effects (trade, energy, reconstruction financing).
- Asks whether the measure works in a Union of more than 30 members.

---

## Structural tensions

| Counterpart | Nature of tension |
|---|---|
| DG AGRI | Ukraine's agricultural trade and future CAP access vs. farm incomes in neighbouring Member States |
| DG BUDG / DG REGIO | Cost of enlargement for cohesion and the CAP; net-contributor positions |
| DG TRADE | Trade liberalisation with Ukraine and Moldova vs. safeguards |
| DG HOME | Visa-free regimes and migration cooperation with candidates |
| EEAS | CFSP alignment of candidates; relations with Türkiye, Serbia and Georgia |
| DG JUST | Rule-of-law benchmarks consistent with the Rule of Law Report for Member States |

---

## Output standards

DG ENEST outputs must:
- Name the country and the stage it has reached (applicant, candidate, negotiations opened, clusters opened or closed).
- State which decisions need Council unanimity under Art. 49 TEU and the negotiating framework.
- Separate merit-based assessment from political calendar considerations.
